page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-80 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configuration built on dedicated Intel x86_64 hardware. It supplies 80 virtual CPUs derived from 40 physical processor cores with two threads per core, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation stands at 640.0 GB, representing an expanded density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or bundled GPUs, relying on attached storage volumes for persistent data. Instruction extensions include Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), AVX-512 vector execution, and hardware cryptography acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute and data manipulation capabilities paired with high memory bus capacity. The processor architecture achieves 65691.98 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 19151.0 in Geekbench multi-core benchmarks, despite moderate single-threaded figures. Uncached memory operations achieve 287.76 GB/sec for large-block reads and 123.61 GB/sec for writes. In-memory data throughput is highlighted by 87.88 million operations per second on Redis SET tests, alongside static web serving throughput reaching 107.93 GB/sec. Specialized matrix registers also support CPU-based inference workloads, processing 254.29 prompt tokens per second on medium 7B parameter language models.

From a resource allocation perspective, this profile provides high memory density per vCPU without dedicating expenditure to attached local disks or discrete accelerators. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external disk bandwidth for storage-heavy tasks, focusing the value proposition purely on system memory and multi-core performance. Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-80 is appropriate for distributed in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching tiers, parallel compilation pipelines, image processing, and CPU-bound matrix computation.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-80 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 80 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 40 physical Intel cores, paired with 640 GB of RAM. Designed around an 8 GB per vCPU memory ratio and 260 MB of L3 cache, the platform incorporates Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions for enhanced vector and matrix calculations. Hardware testing indicates strong multi-threaded execution, registering 65691.98 on multi-core stress-ng benchmarks and 287.76 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. The instance omits local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, focusing architectural resources entirely on main memory density and core concurrency. Realized throughput includes 87.88 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 107.93 GB/sec in static web serving. This hardware configuration is tailored for large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, compilation clusters, image transformation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
